title: VPBank Hanoi International Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
meta_description: VPBank Hanoi International Marathon review: 11,000 runners on 26 October 2025, an AIMS-certified route past 30+ landmarks, and fast Vietnamese winners.
dek: Hanoi's VPBank marathon took about 11,000 runners past Hoan Kiem Lake, Long Bien Bridge and the Old Quarter in October 2025. Here is what that edition was like, and what it tells you about the 2026 race.
verdict: The VPBank Hanoi International Marathon is a heritage tour of the capital on an AIMS-certified course. The 2025 edition, on 26 October, drew about 11,000 runners from 25 countries past more than 30 landmarks, including Hoan Kiem Lake, Long Bien Bridge, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Opera House [1]. The front of the race was fast and Vietnamese: Huynh Anh Khoi won in a personal best of 2:25:15 and former SEA Games champion Pham Thi Hong Le in 2:53:57 [1]. The expo drew more than 50,000 visitors over three days [1]. If you want a big city marathon in Vietnam that shows you Hanoi, this is a strong choice.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: About 11,000 runners from 25 countries took part on Sunday 26 October 2025, on AIMS-certified routes [1]. The courses passed more than 30 of the city's landmarks and historic sites, including Hoan Kiem Lake, Long Bien Bridge, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the Opera House and a corner of the Old Quarter [1].
The race ran alongside a three-day expo, which more than 50,000 athletes, supporters and visitors attended, with a live music night, product tests and games [1].

sections.heading: The Front of the Race
paragraphs: Huynh Anh Khoi won the men's marathon in 2:25:15, about two minutes faster than he had run a month earlier, ahead of SEA Games 5,000 m and 10,000 m champion Nguyen Van Lai (2:26:11) [1]. Former SEA Games 10,000 m champion Pham Thi Hong Le ran alone for almost the whole race and won the women's in 2:53:57, a time that put her in the top 15 overall [1].
In the half marathon, Japan's Makino Saeki won the men's race in 1:13:02 and Nguyen Khanh Ly the women's in 1:25:07 [1].

sections.heading: A Charity Finish
paragraphs: Each finisher contributed VND 30,000 to a fund to plant bamboo against flooding in Nghe An province, and about 7,000 runners hung their bibs on a Prosperity Tree at the finish, raising nearly VND 200 million [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a marathon that doubles as a tour of Hanoi. The certified course, the landmarks and an international field of 11,000 make it a headline race in the capital.
Plan for a big-event weekend: a three-day expo, large crowds and road closures across the centre. Book accommodation near the start early.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the VPBank Hanoi International Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: About 11,000 runners from 25 countries took part on Sunday 26 October 2025. The race's three-day expo drew more than 50,000 athletes, supporters and visitors, and about 7,000 finishers hung their bibs on the finish-area Prosperity Tree for charity.

faqs.question: What is the VPBank Hanoi International Marathon route like?
faqs.answer: A tour of Hanoi's heritage. In 2025 the AIMS-certified courses passed more than 30 landmarks and historic sites, including Hoan Kiem Lake, Long Bien Bridge, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the Hanoi Opera House and part of the Old Quarter.

faqs.question: Who won the VPBank Hanoi International Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: Huynh Anh Khoi won the men's marathon in a personal best of 2:25:15, ahead of Nguyen Van Lai, and Pham Thi Hong Le won the women's in 2:53:57. Japan's Makino Saeki and Nguyen Khanh Ly won the half marathons.
